mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior 3 months indicates expanding economic output, which typically leads to stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO has risen over the prior 3 months, or the correlation between INDPRO trend and SPX returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0 percent, it signals a weakening labor market that may lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0, or the average 20-day return in these instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) coupled with a low year-over-year CPI growth rate (CPIAUCSL growth < 2.0% YoY) indicates a disinflationary environment where the central bank is likely to reduce interest rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the average return in these instances is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions, a housing starts (HOUST) level exceeding 2000 thousand units indicates robust consumer demand for housing, which typically translates to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances during late-cycle expansions when HOUST > 2000, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior 3 months reflects strengthening labor market conditions, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS has increased over the prior 3 months, or the correlation between PAYEMS trend and SPX returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals accelerating inflation that may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL growth > 3.0% YoY, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages indicates strong consumer demand across multiple sectors, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing expansion phase, a rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above 115.0 indicates robust output growth, associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances during manufacturing expansion phases when INDPRO > 115.0, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
